name: Kenya
summary_text: Consensual sex between men is a criminal offence in Kenya under the colonial-era Penal Code, carrying imprisonment of up to 14 years, and the provision is applied regardless of the nationality of those involved. No Kenyan statute governs gender identity, and there is no codified pathway for legal gender recognition; intersex people are legally recognised as a third gender, according to the UK Home Office country policy and information note of February 2025.  Legal gender recognition is obstructed in practice. Evidence before the Milimani High Court in Nairobi, in a decision delivered on 20 May 2026 by Justice Bahati Mwamuye in Petition 27 of 2020, showed that 94 per cent of trans and gender-diverse Kenyans had been refused by civil registration offices, with some applicants spending close to four years' wages on document corrections that failed. Kenya has never had a codified legal framework for gender recognition.  Courts have ordered state action. On 12 August 2025 the Eldoret High Court directed the Kenyan government to enact a Transgender Protection Rights Act, after finding that prisons fail dignity and privacy protections; the petition was brought by a trans Kenyan subjected to non-consensual medical procedures and a court-ordered 'gender determination' while incarcerated.  Police harassment is routine for trans people. Twenty-six interviewees in Mombasa and Nairobi described detention on pretexts such as being drunk and disorderly, on-the-spot extortion demands of 5,000 shillings, and the practice of using traditionally male names as pseudonyms to move through public life safely amid widespread anti-LGBTQ+ sentiment.  Violence against LGBT people is documented and sometimes lethal. In December 2024 a Kenyan man was sentenced to 50 years in jail for killing an LGBTQ activist. The Kenya Human Rights Commission's 'Lives on the Line' report of September 2025, produced with more than 14 community organisations, is the first comprehensive documentation of human-rights violations against sexual and gender minorities in Kenya, covering October 2023 to September 2024; it explicitly challenges the 2019 High Court ruling in Petition 16 of 2019 that dismissed LGBTIQ+ violence claims for purported lack of evidence.  LGBTI civil-society groups may register and operate, but only within a restrictive civic space. The Mombasa Court of Appeal ruled in 2018 that forced anal testing was unconstitutional, with compensation awarded in 2024, and the Supreme Court upheld freedom of association in 2023, allowing LGBTQ organisation registration; a petition against incitement to hatred and discrimination remains before the courts. Societal discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation is widespread and has caused loss of employment and education.

sources.title: Eric Gitari v Attorney General & another (Petition no. 150 of 2016) - High Court of Kenya ruling 24 May 2019
sources.documents: Failed decriminalization challenge to Sections 162(a)(c) and 165; court refused to declare them unconstitutional.
sources.detail: Filed 2016 by NGLHRC executive director Eric Gitari; heard 22-23 Feb 2018; ruling delayed from 22 Feb 2019 to 24 May 2019; appeal noted; Court of Appeal hearing scheduled May 2026

sources.title: Court of Appeal in Mombasa - ruling 22 March 2018 on forced anal examinations
sources.documents: Enforcement practice: forced anal exams, HIV/hepatitis B tests on accused gay men ruled unconstitutional, reversing 2016 High Court decision.
sources.detail: Case from Feb 2015 arrest of two men in Kwale County, exams at Mombasa's Madaraka Hospital; filed by National Gay and Lesbian Human Rights Commission (NGLHRC); related halted exam at Kangundo Level 4 hospital / Kangundo magistrate court

sources.title: High Court of Kenya - August 2025 transgender rights ruling
sources.documents: Landmark trans rights finding: violations of freedom from torture/cruel treatment, equality/non-discrimination, dignity, freedom/security of person, privacy unconstitutional.
sources.detail: Ordered parliament to enact 'Transgender Protection Rights Act, or, in the alternative, amendments of the Intersex Persons Bill 2024'

sources.title: Kenya Human Rights Commission - 2011 report on LGBTI persons
sources.documents: Enforcement abuse despite few convictions under Sec.162-165: police harassment, remand beyond constitutional period, trumped-up charges, extortion/blackmail, bribes/sexual favours, rape by officers.
sources.detail: Cited as Kenya Human Rights Commission reported in 2011; includes quote on LGBTI sex workers mostly MSMs asked for bribes and sexual favours

sources.title: Kenya National Commission on Human Rights - April 2012 report
sources.documents: Trans-specific rights machinery failure: stigma/discrimination, no access to gender re-assignment therapy, detention-cell and bathroom risks, identity problems.
sources.detail: Cites witness denied surgery by Kenyatta National Hospital, failed appeal to Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentist's Board; no statutory provisions for transgender rights / no legal means to change gender

sources.title: Family Protection Bill - National Assembly file ref DLS/NA/BILLS/2/18/2023
sources.documents: Pending escalation risk: would punish 'aggravated homosexuality' with death, criminalize promotion, restrict privacy/assembly/pride parades, monitor spaces, remove LGBTQ topics from curricula, overturn 2023 Supreme Court association-rights decision.
sources.detail: Written/introduced 2023 by MP George Peter Opondo Kaluma; inspired by Uganda Anti-Homosexuality Act; before Committee on Social Protection for pre-publication scrutiny for ~2 years
